reading.body:
Most New Jersey data center capacity remains undisclosed. CyrusOne Totowa's 6 MW is one of only five facilities in the state whose operators publish power specifications, making it part of a sparse and unrepresentative sample of the state's 48 mapped facilities.

New Jersey sits in the densest data center region in the United States, where grid access is heavily contested. The state announces 111.3 MW of IT capacity across disclosed facilities, and Totowa accounts for 5.4% of that total. This concentration matters because power availability, not facility space, now constrains AI deployment. The undisclosed majority of New Jersey's 48 facilities could hold substantially more capacity than the announced figure suggests, or substantially less. The reading depends entirely on whether operators choose to publish.

Totowa's 6 MW translates to roughly 150 racks at typical AI training density. The facility is certified for SSAE 16 Type II compliance. This tells nothing about whether the site has power or cooling headroom to expand, whether it connects to resilient grid capacity, or whether it serves hyperscale training workloads or smaller enterprise use cases. It also does not reveal how many of New Jersey's other 47 unmeasured facilities are similarly modest, or whether the undisclosed ones are larger.
